newsitem.title: USA: S. Carolina jobless rate dips to 5.9 pct in August.
newsitem.headline: S. Carolina jobless rate dips to 5.9 pct in August.

text.p: South Carolina's unemployment rate declined slightly to 5.9 percent in August from 6 percent in July, the state Employment Security Commission said Wednesday.
The state added 5,600 jobs during the month, putting total nonfarm employment at 1.68 million.

Government posted the largest gain, 2,200 jobs, as schools and colleges began preparing for the fall term. Trade increased by 1,600 jobs and services gained 1,100. Transporation and public utilities added 500 jobs while finance, insurance and real estate gained 300. Construction lost 100 jobs and was the only major sector to report a decrease.

"We expect little change in the economy over the next few months," said commission Executive Director Robert David. "State and local schools will pick up jobs as restaffing continues but tourist-related losses in trade and services will likely keep the jobless rate at round 6 percent."
Beaufort County had the state's lowest unemployment rate for August, 3 percent, while Marlboro County had the highest, 16.3 percent.
